hpi: {{patient_name}} is a man who recently returned from a cruise ship and presents with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, jaundice, and shortness of breath. He has RUQ tenderness on exam. LFTs are markedly elevated in the 2000-3000 range. The cruise ship travel and profoundly elevated transaminases are highly suspicious for acute viral hepatitis A (fecal-oral transmission). His episodes of vomiting led to aspiration pneumonia. Acetaminophen level should be checked to rule out overdose as a cause of acute liver injury. Management is supportive: IV fluids, antiemetics, oxygen for hypoxia, and antibiotics for aspiration pneumonia per ATS/IDSA guidelines (treat as community-acquired pneumonia; no anaerobic coverage needed without abscess/empyema). Acetaminophen is contraindicated with hepatic injury. Admit to inpatient unit.
